report.summary: Audit of graph_delta.py fitness function. Key findings: (1) 75.3% detection is inflated by including 'code.refs.leaky' layer which detects marker comments (SEEDED DEFECT) — true clean-arm detection is lower. (2) change_constant scores 0/62 because it only changes data literals; the 'literals' layer uses repr() which for strings like 'claude_cli' is identical before/after (repr('claude_cli') == "'claude_cli'"), so no delta. (3) Operator mix bias: corpus is 300 mutants but only 62 are 'change_constant' — the rest are deletions/insertions that move AST refs or structure. (4) Specificity arm (real
risks: Leaky layer (code.refs.leaky) includes comment tokens, so marker words 'SEEDED DEFECT' cause false detections. This inflates the headline number.

change_constant mutants are invisible to the 'literals' layer because repr() of string literals is identical before/after (e.g., 'claude_cli' vs 'claude_cli' both repr to "'claude_cli'"). The multiset key uses repr, so no delta.
Corpus is 300 mutants but only 62 are change_constant; the rest are deletions/insertions that naturally move AST refs or structure. This operator mix bias inflates overall detection rate.
Specificity arm (real commits) is not fully implemented in the excerpt; without it, false alarm rate is unknown.
todos: Run clean arm (SCORING_LAYERS excluding 'code.refs.leaky') on full corpus and report detected/applied. Compare to headline 75.3%.
Fix 'literals' layer to detect changes in string literal values (e.g., compare raw values, not repr).
Complete specificity arm (measure_commit) to measure false alarm rate on real commits.
Report detection rate per defect class separately, especially change_constant.

handoff.suggestion: To falsify the headline claim, run `python -c "from daedalus.eval.graph_delta import run; rep = run(); print(rep['detected'], '/', rep['applied'])"` and compare to 75.3%. If detected/applied < 75.3%, the leaky layer inflated the number. Also check that change_constant mutants are 0/62 in the clean arm.
